question: In the theatre team, who is mainly responsible for writing down the counts on the whiteboard?

options.A: The lead surgeon
options.B: The scrub nurse
options.C: The anesthetist
options.D: The circulating nurse

explanation: The circulating nurse is outside the sterile field (unsterile zone), which makes them the perfect person to maintain the official tally board.

question: Which of the following is NOT true about integrating different types of healthcare plans?

options.A: Alignment between plans helps prevent wasted resources
options.B: Nurse managers must communicate both upward and downward
options.C: Strategic, tactical, and operational plans must work together
options.D: Operational plans can completely contradict strategic goals without consequence

explanation: Operational plans must support strategic goals, not contradict them, for the organization to succeed. [learn more](GST321_U1_T6#GST321_U1_T6_h6)

question: A nurse wants to check if a patient truly understands their new blood pressure medicine. Which question is best to ask?

options.A: Do you understand all the instructions on this prescription label?
options.B: Will you remember to swallow this tablet every single morning?
options.C: Is there anything confusing about this blood pressure medication?
options.D: Can you explain to me how and when you will take this pill at home?

explanation: Asking the patient to explain the instructions in their own words (the teach-back method) reveals their true understanding better than a simple yes-or-no question. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T3#GNS125_U3_T3_h3)

question: Why do many rural families traditionally view having many children as a great benefit?

options.A: The government pays monthly stipends for large households
options.B: Children provide farm labor and security in old age
options.C: Larger households receive free agricultural land allotments
options.D: School fees are fully subsidized for families with five children

explanation: Spot on! In farming communities, children help out on the farm and support their parents as they grow older.

question: Why must the tools used to cut the umbilical cord be strictly sterile?

options.A: To follow trendy hospital equipment rules
options.B: To make the cutting smooth and fast for the midwife
options.C: To keep the scissors from getting stained
options.D: To prevent serious infections like neonatal tetanus

explanation: A newborn's belly button is a direct doorway for germs, so keeping cutting tools sterile is a total lifesaving must!

question: Why is poor communication among healthcare team members dangerous during obstetric emergencies?

options.A: It increases the cost of laboratory reagents in the hospital
options.B: It can cause dangerous delays in life-saving interventions
options.C: It automatically invalidates the patient's health insurance policy
options.D: It prevents nurses from writing shift reports in the register

explanation: Delays in sharing vital clinical information during an emergency can stall urgent treatment and worsen maternal outcomes. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T15#GNS225_U3_T15_h4)

question: A patient arrives at the clinic with recurring kidney stones and severe flank pain. Which diagnostic test is most appropriate to visualize the exact location of the stones in the ureters?

options.A: Intravenous pyelogram
options.B: Electrocardiogram
options.C: Pulmonary function test
options.D: Echocardiogram

explanation: An IVP uses contrast dye to highlight the urinary tract, making it very effective for spotting kidney stones causing flank pain. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is the best home care approach for managing a mild diaper rash?

options.A: Keeping the skin clean, dry, and applying a barrier ointment
options.B: Covering the rash tightly with plastic-lined pants
options.C: Scrubbing the affected area with perfumed soap daily
options.D: Applying strong prescription steroid creams immediately

explanation: Great choice! Diaper rash clears up fastest when you keep the skin dry, change diapers frequently, and use a soothing barrier cream.

question: Which type of lung cancer is the most commonly diagnosed in clinical practice?

options.A: Bronchial Carcinoid Tumor
options.B: Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
options.C: Small Cell Lung Cancer
options.D: Primary Pleural Mesothelioma

explanation: You've got this! Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer accounts for about 85% of all lung cancer cases, making it much more common than the small cell type.

question: What happens when someone's line of gravity moves outside their base of support?

options.A: Muscle strength instantly doubles
options.B: Blood pressure drops to zero
options.C: Joint flexibility increases
options.D: The person loses balance and falls

explanation: Spot on! If your center of balance wanders outside your footing, gravity takes over and down you go. That's why wide stances keep us steady.

question: What do we call a normal, smooth, and uncomplicated labour and delivery?

options.A: Placenta praevia
options.B: Eutocia
options.C: Cephalopelvic disproportion
options.D: Dystocia

explanation: You've got this! Eutocia is just the medical word for a normal, straightforward delivery, while dystocia means a difficult labour. Easy peasy!

question: What are the classic warning signs of acute postpartum endometritis?

options.A: Lower abdominal pain and fever
options.B: Sudden weight gain and swelling
options.C: Itching and burning during urination
options.D: Complete loss of appetite and nausea

explanation: Always watch out for a fever and lower tummy pain in new mothers—these are the big red flags telling us the uterus might be infected.

question: Why is a tension pneumothorax such a major emergency?

options.A: Trapped air builds up pressure and shifts the heart and major blood vessels
options.B: It stops the kidneys from producing urine within minutes
options.C: It floods both lungs with thick, yellow mucus
options.D: It causes an immediate massive infection in the bronchial tubes

explanation: Correct! Trapped air keeps stacking up like a balloon, pushing everything in the chest sideways and stopping blood from returning to the heart.

question: What is the primary overarching goal of Nigeria's National Population Policy?

options.A: Halting all immigration into the country immediately
options.B: Reducing the national literacy rate to save government funds
options.C: Eliminating the entire rural population through urbanization
options.D: Improving the standard of living and quality of life for citizens

explanation: At its heart, every goal in the population policy is about making sure citizens live healthier, better-quality lives by balancing population growth with available resources.

question: Why is psychosocial support so important in internally displaced persons (IDP) camps?

options.A: To teach residents advanced corporate business management
options.B: To help residents cope with the mental trauma of displacement and loss
options.C: To replace the need for clean drinking water
options.D: To make sure people follow commercial tax rules

explanation: Spot on! Losing your home and community causes deep emotional pain. Mental health and psychosocial support are crucial for true healing and recovery.

question: A patient living near farm animals comes in with a suspected zoonotic infection. What is the best health advice to give them?

options.A: Tell them never to take medications for animal scratches
options.B: Suggest getting rid of every single animal in the neighborhood
options.C: Teach them safe food handling and how to protect themselves around animals
options.D: Tell them humans only catch things from other humans

explanation: Good hygiene, safe food prep, and protective gear go a long way in keeping animal germs away from humans.

question: During the final delivery of the baby's body, which part usually comes out first?

options.A: The posterior hip
options.B: The umbilical cord
options.C: The anterior shoulder
options.D: The lower extremities

explanation: Spot on! The front shoulder slips out from under the pubic bone first, and then the back shoulder follows.

question: Why is healthy, unbroken skin considered part of the innate immune system?

options.A: It contains mature T-lymphocytes that destroy foreign organisms
options.B: It acts as a physical barrier that stops pathogens from entering the body
options.C: It actively manufactures specific antibodies against local skin bacteria
options.D: It produces high levels of inflammatory cytokines during minor scrapes

explanation: Spot on! Your skin is your body's first wall of defense, stopping germs from getting inside in the first place.

question: Why do the liver and kidneys suffer damage from toxins more often than other organs?

options.A: They are located closest to the digestive tract where toxins enter
options.B: They have thick protective walls that trap circulating poisons inside them
options.C: They produce natural antibodies that chemically react with heavy metals
options.D: They process, filter, and concentrate large volumes of blood in the body

explanation: Since these are the body's main cleaning and filtering organs, they naturally handle the highest amounts of circulating toxins.

question: When are helicopter or boat transport methods most necessary during a disaster evacuation?

options.A: When floods, landslides, or collapsed bridges block traditional roads
options.B: When the patient has a minor injury and lives next to a hospital
options.C: When hospital emergency rooms are completely empty
options.D: When ground ambulances are running low on diesel fuel only

explanation: Spot on! When roads are completely impassable due to natural disasters, air and water transport are the only ways out.

question: Which environmental hazard should be removed from a room to protect a patient with a mobility impairment?

options.A: Heavy wooden wardrobes
options.B: Overhead ceiling lights
options.C: Loose throw rugs
options.D: Wall-mounted handrails

explanation: Loose rugs slip easily under feet or mobility devices, making them a leading cause of preventable indoor falls. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T10#GNS225_U5_T10_h8)

question: What important safety rule must nurses follow when discussing research on social media?

options.A: They must ensure their posts are at least ten pages long
options.B: They must strictly protect patient privacy and confidentiality at all times
options.C: They must use only Latin medical terms in their messages
options.D: They are required to pay a tax on every scientific post they share

explanation: Online sharing carries risks of breaching privacy, so nurses must never reveal identifying patient details. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T2#GNS224_U4_T2_h7)

question: When cleaning a hospital ward, why should you always clean from high areas to low areas, and clean zones to dirty zones?

options.A: To ensure that heavy cleaning buckets stay balanced on wheeled carts
options.B: To prevent dirt and pathogens from falling onto already cleaned surfaces
options.C: To reduce the total amount of chemical spray needed for the room
options.D: To speed up the chemical evaporation rate across large ward floors

explanation: Working top-to-bottom stops gravity from dropping dust and germs right back onto the spots you just finished cleaning!

question: What is a big advantage of making drugs in a lab instead of harvesting plants?

options.A: It is not dependent on weather or farming seasons
options.B: It eliminates the need for any quality control testing
options.C: It guarantees that the drug will never cause side effects
options.D: It makes the medication completely free for all hospitals

explanation: Lab-made drugs mean we never have to worry about droughts, poor crop yields, or animal diseases disrupting our medicine supply.

question: Why should you tell a patient that a steroid nasal spray won't clear a stuffy nose instantly like a decongestant spray?

options.A: The body destroys steroid medications before they reach the tissue.
options.B: Steroids work slowly by altering cellular processes over days, not minutes.
options.C: Steroid molecules are too large to absorb through the nasal lining quickly.
options.D: Nasal sprays only work if the patient tilts their head upside down.

explanation: You're right! Steroids change gene expression and protein making inside cells, which takes a few days to show real magic. Patience is key with these sprays!

question: During which phase of the PDSA cycle do you actually carry out your new idea on a small scale?

options.A: Do phase
options.B: Act phase
options.C: Study phase
options.D: Plan phase

explanation: The 'Do' phase is where the action happens! You test your idea on the ward and see how it works in real life.

question: Which side effect do many patients report during the first few weeks of taking an Efavirenz-based regimen?

options.A: Vivid dreams or dizziness
options.B: Permanent blindness
options.C: Complete loss of hearing
options.D: Sudden hair color changes

explanation: Correct! Efavirenz can temporarily cause quirky side effects like vivid dreams or feeling dizzy, but these usually fade away after the first few weeks.

question: Why does an RCA team repeatedly ask 'why' an incident occurred?

options.A: To delay reporting the incident to hospital executives for as long as possible
options.B: To prove that the patient contributed to their own injury
options.C: To interrogate nurses until they admit fault for their careless actions
options.D: To trace the chain of events back to the fundamental systemic breakdown

explanation: Asking 'why' multiple times peels back superficial layers of error to expose the real root cause in the workflow or environment. [learn more](GST319_U6_T1#GST319_U6_T1_h4)

question: Which type of ovarian cancer is the most common, making up about 90% of all cases?

options.A: Germ cell tumors
options.B: Stromal cell tumors
options.C: Endodermal sinus tumors
options.D: Epithelial ovarian cancer

explanation: Spot on! Epithelial tumors start from the outer surface lining of the ovary and make up the vast majority of cases we see in practice.

question: Which infant condition is Bryant's traction typically used to treat?

options.A: Spina bifida complications
options.B: Severe clubfoot deformity
options.C: Fractured clavicle from birth
options.D: Congenital hip dislocation

explanation: Bryant's traction gently lifts both of a baby's legs straight up in the air to help realign a dislocated hip. Nursing pediatrics made simple!

question: A staff nurse wants to learn advanced wound care techniques and earn a promotion to ward sister. What do these desires represent?

options.A: Statutory penalties
options.B: Financial liabilities
options.C: Personal objectives
options.D: Organisational mandates

explanation: Spot on! Wanting to learn new skills and climb the career ladder are classic examples of personal goals you set for your own nursing career.

question: Why are patients with nephrotic syndrome at a much higher risk for blood clots?

options.A: They lie in bed all day without moving their legs
options.B: Their red blood cell count increases drastically
options.C: They lose clotting-regulatory proteins through their urine
options.D: Their blood pressure is always extremely high

explanation: The kidneys filter out proteins that normally prevent blood from clotting too easily, leaving the blood in a hypercoagulable state. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T8#GNS213_U4_T8_h6)

question: What is the primary goal of conducting regular nursing documentation audits in a health facility?

options.A: To find reasons to suspend nurses who make minor spelling mistakes
options.B: To collect extra money from clients during home visits
options.C: To evaluate the quality of care and ensure compliance with professional standards
options.D: To reduce the number of clients admitted to the community program

explanation: Audits help identify gaps in clinical practice and documentation, guiding continuous quality improvement in patient care. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h8)

question: What is the main goal of a Patient Classification System?

options.A: To calculate annual facility building taxes
options.B: To categorize patients based on their nursing care needs
options.C: To track hospital utility and electricity usage
options.D: To determine which doctors are on emergency call

explanation: It sorts patients by how sick they are (acuity) so hospitals can figure out how much nursing time is truly required.

question: At what age is the initial virological diagnostic test (DNA PCR) recommended for an HIV-exposed infant?

options.A: At 6 weeks of age or earliest possible contact
options.B: Immediately upon delivery before leaving the labor ward
options.C: At 18 months of age after breastfeeding completely stops
options.D: At 5 years of age before starting primary school

explanation: DNA PCR testing is recommended around 6 weeks of age to detect the genetic material of the virus early and start treatment if positive. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h6)

question: What is the primary role of skeletal muscles during ambulation?

options.A: Contracting to pull bones and create motion
options.B: Sending electrical signals to the brain
options.C: Producing red blood cells for oxygen transport
options.D: Absorbing shock within the joint spaces

explanation: Skeletal muscles shorten and pull on bones across joints to move the body forward during walking. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T8#GNS324_U3_T8_h2)

question: What is the single biggest preventable cause of chronic lung disease (COPD) worldwide?

options.A: Childhood asthma attacks
options.B: Inhaling coal dust at work
options.C: Smoke from indoor cooking fires
options.D: Tobacco smoke exposure

explanation: Tobacco smoke is tough on the airways and air sacs over time. Because people can choose to avoid or quit it, it stands out as the number one preventable cause of COPD globally.

question: How do you check a baby's head sutures and fontanelles during a vaginal examination?

options.A: Shining a specialized light beam through the maternal abdomen
options.B: Measuring the external abdominal girth with a tape measure
options.C: Listening for echoes with a wooden stethoscope
options.D: Palpating the presenting part with a sterile gloved finger

explanation: You gently feel (palpate) the baby's head using a sterile gloved finger during an internal check to identify the fontanelles and sutures.

question: How does adrenaline directly affect blood flow to the uterus when a mum is stressed?

options.A: It stops all electrical activity in the myometrium instantly
options.B: It dilates blood vessels to increase oxygen delivery to the fetus
options.C: It converts glucose into amniotic fluid rapidly
options.D: It constricts blood vessels and reduces blood flow to the uterus

explanation: Stress hormones cause blood vessels to tighten up (vasoconstriction), drawing blood away from the womb and sending it to the big muscles instead.

question: Why is teaching the family so important before sending a neuro client home?

options.A: Clients with brain injuries never regain their memory or thinking skills
options.B: Family members are legally required to pass a written nursing exam
options.C: Caregivers need to recognize warning signs of complications and manage daily care
options.D: Home health nurses are not allowed to visit clients after discharge

explanation: Since family members will be doing the heavy lifting at home, they need to know what red flags mean it's time to rush back to the hospital.

question: At what angle should your needle enter the skin to create a smooth, curved stitch?

options.A: A downward 45-degree angle
options.B: A flat 15-degree angle
options.C: A completely parallel angle
options.D: A perpendicular 90-degree angle

explanation: Entering at a 90-degree angle lets the curved needle follow its natural circular shape, making it glide right through the skin smoothly.

question: Which of these is NOT a common sign of meningitis?

options.A: High fever and body chills
options.B: Sudden complete paralysis of the lower limbs
options.C: Severe and pounding headache
options.D: Stiff and painful neck movement

explanation: Spot on! Meningitis causes terrible headaches, fever, and a stiff neck, but leg paralysis is not a standard sign of the infection.

question: Which nursing action helps prevent deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in a paralyzed leg?

options.A: Keeping the legs elevated above the heart all day
options.B: Massaging the calf muscles vigorously every hour
options.C: Encouraging regular leg movement and compression stockings
options.D: Restricting fluid intake to decrease blood volume

explanation: Movement and compression help keep the blood flowing so it doesn't pool and form dangerous clots! (Never massage a red, swollen calf—that could dislodge a clot!)

question: Which nursing action directly helps get rid of germs on hands and hospital equipment?

options.A: Allowing visitors to share food freely with patients
options.B: Practicing strict hand hygiene and clean techniques
options.C: Discharging all admitted patients right away
options.D: Turning off the AC units in the rooms

explanation: Good hand washing and clean hospital habits sweep away germs before they can set up camp and infect someone.

question: Why do patients with atrial fibrillation need anticoagulant medications?

options.A: To normalize a rapid irregular heart rate
options.B: To prevent stroke caused by blood clots in the atria
options.C: To dissolve fatty plaque buildup in coronary arteries
options.D: To lower systemic high blood pressure levels

explanation: In atrial fibrillation, blood can pool in the heart and form clots that might travel to the brain. Thinners protect them from strokes!

question: Which needle gauge is best for a routine subcutaneous injection?

options.A: 32 to 36 gauge
options.B: 20 to 22 gauge
options.C: 25 to 30 gauge
options.D: 14 to 18 gauge

explanation: Higher gauge numbers mean thinner needles! A 25 to 30 gauge needle slips in smoothly and keeps the injection as painless as possible.

question: Which of these is an example of biochemical data collected during a nutrition check?

options.A: Presence of muscle wasting
options.B: Body Mass Index score
options.C: Serum albumin levels
options.D: Daily water intake diary

explanation: You got it! Lab tests like serum albumin give us hard biochemical facts about protein levels inside the body.

question: You are filling out a referral form for a pregnant mum with severe pre-eclampsia. What is the most important clinical finding to write down?

options.A: Her personal opinion about hospital food quality
options.B: The distance from her house to the primary healthcare center
options.C: The name of her local community youth organization
options.D: Her most recent blood pressure reading and urine protein test

explanation: Brilliant! Vital signs like her BP and protein levels give the incoming delivery and doctor team immediate, life-saving information.

question: Why is psychological safety important for nursing staff?

options.A: It prevents patients from ever experiencing any clinical complications
options.B: It guarantees that nurses will receive a salary increase every year
options.C: It allows nurses to report near misses and errors without fear of unfair punishment
options.D: It eliminates the need for doctors to supervise nursing procedures

explanation: When nurses feel safe from unfair punishment, they freely report near misses. This helps the whole team spot hazards and keep patients safe.

question: Why is getting enough protein so crucial during the body's recovery phase after surgery?

options.A: It acts as a mild pain reliever for the surgical wound
options.B: It prevents the patient from experiencing low blood pressure
options.C: It stops the endocrine system from releasing stress hormones
options.D: It provides the amino acids needed to rebuild broken down muscle and repair incisions

explanation: Right! Protein supplies the building blocks (amino acids) needed to close wounds and rebuild tissues after the body has broken them down.

question: What is the primary focus of safe motherhood initiatives?

options.A: Ensuring a healthy pregnancy and safe childbirth for every woman
options.B: Providing free formula feeding to all newborns
options.C: Increasing the birth rate in rural communities
options.D: Eliminating the need for traditional birth attendants

explanation: Safe motherhood focuses directly on the health and survival of women throughout pregnancy, delivery, and the postpartum period. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T44#GNS214_U1_T44_h1)

question: What does 'cultural negotiation' mean when caring for patients at home?

options.A: Trading hospital supplies for traditional ceremonial artifacts
options.B: Convincing the client to stop all cultural practices immediately
options.C: Blending harmless traditional remedies with modern medical care
options.D: Letting the client manage their disease entirely without medicine

explanation: Well done! Cultural negotiation means finding a safe middle ground—respecting their traditions while keeping them safe with modern care.

question: Which gene mutations are most strongly linked to a higher risk of ovarian cancer?

options.A: BRCA1 and BRCA2
options.B: HER2 and KRAS
options.C: TP53 and EGFR
options.D: APC and MLH1

explanation: Spot on. Inherited mutations in the BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes significantly increase a woman's lifetime chance of developing both breast and ovarian cancers.

question: Which nursing action best describes a promotive reproductive health service?

options.A: Suturing a perineal tear following a normal vaginal delivery
options.B: Performing a manual vacuum aspiration for an incomplete miscarriage
options.C: Leading a community health talk on proper menstrual hygiene
options.D: Prescribing antibiotics for a confirmed pelvic inflammatory disease

explanation: Promotive services involve general health education and encouraging positive wellness practices rather than treating active disease. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h2)

question: Why is a vague phrase like 'improving community health' not ideal as a project indicator?

options.A: It can only be evaluated by international health organizations
options.B: It lacks specific targets and measurable parameters to track progress accurately
options.C: It is too expensive to write down in official government records
options.D: It focuses only on financial expenditures instead of patient care

explanation: If a goal doesn't have clear numbers and timeframes, it's impossible to prove whether things actually got better!

question: Which of these common items can block your body from absorbing oral levothyroxine?

options.A: Antacids containing calcium or aluminum
options.B: Inhaled bronchodilators for asthma
options.C: Broad-spectrum antibiotics like penicillin
options.D: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs

explanation: Minerals like calcium and aluminum act like magnets in your stomach, grabbing onto the levothyroxine and stopping it from entering your blood.

question: What does healthcare outsourcing actually mean?

options.A: Hiring external vendors to perform specific hospital operations or services
options.B: Closing down public health clinics to build private pharmacies
options.C: Permanently selling public hospitals to private business owners
options.D: Transferring clinical nurses to foreign healthcare institutions

explanation: Outsourcing is like hiring an outside expert to handle specific tasks (like security or laundry) while the hospital stays in charge of the big picture.

question: Why is handing project ownership over to local community members crucial for sustainability?

options.A: So the program continues running even after external funding or staff leave
options.B: So the government can tax the community for health services
options.C: So nobody can be held responsible if the project fails
options.D: So nurses can retire and stop working permanently

explanation: When locals own and lead the initiative, the program survives independently of outside organizations and temporary grants. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T7#GNS314_U4_T7_h8)

question: How do the kidneys respond when a patient develops metabolic acidosis?

options.A: They excrete more hydrogen ions and reabsorb bicarbonate
options.B: They reabsorb more hydrogen ions and excrete bicarbonate
options.C: They convert excess acid into glucose in the cortex
options.D: They stop all filtration until blood pH normalizes

explanation: To raise blood pH back to normal, the kidneys get rid of excess acid and keep bicarbonate to buffer the blood. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T1#GNS121_U2_T1_h5)

question: Which strategy is most effective when educating rural community members about pregnancy danger signs?

options.A: Using simple local dialects and relatable community gathering spaces
options.B: Hosting lectures exclusively in urban tertiary teaching hospitals
options.C: Requiring written exams before women can attend antenatal care
options.D: Distributing dense medical journals written in advanced technical terms

explanation: Effective community health education meets people where they are, using familiar language and local venues like markets or places of worship. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T14#GNS225_U3_T14_h5)

question: What is the main goal of public health laws for food businesses?

options.A: To collect high taxes from commercial food business owners
options.B: To limit the number of small restaurants operating in local communities
options.C: To standardize recipe ingredients across different cultural restaurants
options.D: To establish minimum safety and sanitation rules that protect the public

explanation: Public health rules set clear hygiene and facility standards to prevent widespread food poisoning. You've got this down!

question: On a lab report, what does a "shift to the left" in white blood cells usually tell the healthcare team?

options.A: An allergic reaction rather than a bacterial infection
options.B: A recovery phase where all blood counts return to normal
options.C: An increased release of immature white blood cells
options.D: A complete failure of the bone marrow to produce cells

explanation: You nailed it! When a severe infection drains the mature white blood cells, the bone marrow starts rushing out baby cells ('bands') early to help out.

question: Why do health workers draw an epidemic curve on a graph during an outbreak?

options.A: To show the timeline of when cases occurred and track the outbreak's progress
options.B: To prove to international donors that funding was spent wisely
options.C: To measure the physical distance between houses in the village
options.D: To predict exactly what the weather will be like next week

explanation: Brilliant! An epidemic curve turns dates into a picture, helping investigators see when infections started and whether the outbreak is slowing down or growing.

question: Why is just treating medical symptoms often not enough for a community?

options.A: Patients refuse to visit primary health care clinics unless accompanied by local leaders
options.B: Environmental and social root causes like poor water or housing will keep causing new illnesses
options.C: Doctors usually prescribe the wrong medications for community outbreaks
options.D: Medical treatments are too expensive for the government to maintain long-term

explanation: Spot on! If we treat a patient in the clinic but send them back to drink contaminated water, they'll just fall sick again. We have to fix the environment too!

question: Which of the following is a direct health function of the PTA?

options.A: Stocking the school clinic with first aid materials
options.B: Performing surgical operations during emergencies
options.C: Prescribing antibiotics to sick students in class
options.D: Teaching all the mathematics lessons in school

explanation: Providing basic first aid supplies is a practical way the PTA helps manage minor health issues in school. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T5#GNS225_U4_T5_h2)

question: Why can't nurses rely on regular surgical masks when caring for patients with airborne diseases?

options.A: Surgical masks trap moisture and destroy bacterial filters
options.B: Pathogens are small enough to pass through regular mask material
options.C: Droplet nuclei can easily bypass loose-fitting surgical masks
options.D: Surgical masks only protect against blood splashes

explanation: You've got this! Regular surgical masks aren't tightly sealed enough around the edges, meaning those sneaky floating droplet nuclei can slip right past them.

question: What is the main sign that someone has a drug abuse problem?

options.A: Using vitamins for daily nutritional balance
options.B: Consuming natural herbs for mild headaches
options.C: Harmful or hazardous use despite negative consequences
options.D: Taking prescribed medications strictly as directed

explanation: Drug abuse means a person keeps using a substance even when it clearly harms their health, relationships, or daily life. You've got this!

question: What is the main goal of physical rehabilitation for someone recovering from advanced leprosy?

options.A: Restoring functional independence and improving quality of life
options.B: Accelerating the natural destruction of persistent dormant bacilli
options.C: Replacing all damaged nerve tissue with synthetic nerve grafts
options.D: Eliminating the need for daily skin and eye self-examinations

explanation: You've got it! Rehabilitation is all about helping patients regain their independence, manage disabilities, and live fulfilling lives.

question: A patient with uncontrolled diabetes complains of a constant burning and shooting pain in their feet. What type of pain is this?

options.A: Somatic pain
options.B: Nociceptive pain
options.C: Visceral pain
options.D: Neuropathic pain

explanation: Neuropathic pain comes directly from nerve damage (like from high blood sugar over time). It often feels like burning, tingling, or shooting pain.

question: When a mosquito bites you and passes on the malaria parasite, what kind of transmission is this?

options.A: Contact transmission
options.B: Vehicle-borne transmission
options.C: Vector-borne transmission
options.D: Droplet transmission

explanation: Vectors are living creatures, like mosquitoes or ticks, that carry germs from one person or animal to another. Great clinical connection for Nigerian nursing practice!

question: What is the main job of an umbilical cord clamp?

options.A: To hold the sewing needle steady during repairs
options.B: To safely stop blood flow through the cut cord stump

question: A patient is prescribed a sustained-release capsule for chronic pain. What must the nurse tell the patient about taking this medication?

question: Which of these common chest tube practices is actually dangerous and should be avoided?

explanation: Snap! Snapping open that glass top creates tiny, invisible glass shards. A filter needle acts like a tiny shield, catching those shards so they never make it into the syringe.

question: What major mistake should you avoid when writing the results section?

options.A: Using tables and charts to summarize numerical findings
options.B: Including personal interpretations and opinions about the data
options.C: Reporting findings that go against the original hypothesis
options.D: Stating the exact statistical values found in the study

explanation: Keep the results section strictly factual! Save your opinions and deep meanings for the discussion chapter.

question: Which of these is a major reason why a doctor would order a lumbar puncture?

options.A: Suspected meningitis
options.B: Broken vertebrae
options.C: Severe dehydration
options.D: Muscle spasm

explanation: You got it! Testing cerebrospinal fluid is key to diagnosing central nervous system infections like meningitis.

question: A patient recovering from a long, difficult labor reports a constant, uncontrolled leak of urine from her vagina. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: Vaginal fistula
options.B: Simple rectocele
options.C: Transverse septum
options.D: Imperforate hymen

explanation: That's correct! Prolonged pressure during a tough labor can damage the tissue wall between the bladder and vagina, creating an abnormal opening (a fistula) that leaks urine.

question: Why does the human brain have many folds, or gyri and sulci?

options.A: To separate the left and right hemispheres
options.B: To circulate cerebrospinal fluid faster
options.C: To pack a larger surface area inside the skull
options.D: To protect the brain from physical shock

explanation: Folding allows a massive sheet of brain tissue to fit compactly within the bony limits of the human skull. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T23#GNS211_U3_T23_h1)

question: When is empiric antibiotic therapy usually started for a sick patient?

options.A: Only when the exact microscopic species is confirmed
options.B: After the patient is fully discharged from the hospital
options.C: When the patient shows an allergic reaction to skin tests
options.D: Before laboratory culture results return from the lab

explanation: Empiric treatment gives a patient immediate help based on clinical signs while we wait for the lab results to come back. Great to know for ward practice! [learn more](GST114_U1_T1#GST114_U1_T1_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical challenge when patients try to change their diet?

options.A: Unsupportive family members in the home
options.B: Financial constraints and high food costs
options.C: Excessive availability of free clinical dietitians
options.D: Lack of cooking skills or kitchen facilities

explanation: Correct! Having access to helpful dietitians is a blessing, not a barrier. The real struggles are usually money, time, and kitchen setups. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T005#GNS227_U7_T005_h6)

question: How do health orderlies help control infections in the theatre?

options.A: They wear sterile gowns and handle surgical instruments
options.B: They scrub the surgeon's hands before the operation begins
options.C: They help clean the theatre and dispose of waste between cases
options.D: They sterilize surgical blades inside the autoclave machine

explanation: By clearing waste and cleaning up after procedures, orderlies play a huge part in keeping the theatre safe from hospital-acquired infections.

question: How often should a client receive a DMPA (Depo-Provera) injection for birth control?

options.A: Every 6 months
options.B: Every 1 month
options.C: Every 3 months
options.D: Every 2 months

explanation: You've got this! DMPA gives steady hormonal protection when given once every 3 months (about 13 weeks).

question: A junior nurse is told to do a dressing change a certain way simply because 'that is how we've always done it here.' What type of inquiry is this?

options.A: Traditional and authority-based inquiry
options.B: Randomized controlled testing
options.C: Empirical scientific inquiry
options.D: Systematic qualitative inquiry

explanation: Relying on past custom and instructions from senior staff without checking the literature is traditional and authority-based inquiry.

question: Why is accurate documentation of the screening process vital on the antenatal card?

options.A: It stops the mother from changing her mind about her due date
options.B: It replaces the need to talk to the family during labor
options.C: It ensures the nurse gets a higher salary each month
options.D: It provides continuity of care if another provider takes over

explanation: Written records allow any healthcare worker to quickly see the patient's risk status and history in an emergency. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h8)

question: What is a major goal of financial control when it comes to hospital supplies?

options.A: Resource optimization to prevent unnecessary waste
options.B: Throwing away expired items without tracking
options.C: Hiding extra supplies in locked closets indefinitely
options.D: Buying only the most expensive brands available

explanation: A key goal is using our materials wisely so we avoid waste and keep things running without breaking the bank.

question: What is the best focus for a nurse counseling an adult patient on weight management?

options.A: Recommending strict, low-calorie crash diets for fast numerical weight loss
options.B: Focusing solely on medication options to suppress appetite and boost metabolism
options.C: Encouraging sustainable lifestyle habits like balanced eating and regular physical activity
options.D: Telling the patient to rely exclusively on daily BMI tracking to judge progress

explanation: Great choice! Lasting health wins come from realistic, sustainable lifestyle changes—not punishing crash diets.

question: A newborn delivered after a tough, instrument-assisted birth is very sleepy (lethargic) and has a high-pitched cry. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: Physiological moulding
options.B: Normal post-birth fatigue
options.C: Mild caput succedaneum
options.D: Intracranial hemorrhage

explanation: You nailed it. Unusual sleepiness and a high-pitched cry are classic red flags that there might be pressure or bleeding inside the baby's head.

question: What is one of the main responsibilities of community health workers when it comes to post-natal care?

options.A: Performing major surgical repairs for tears
options.B: Delivering babies in primary operating theatres
options.C: Conducting home visits and tracking immunizations
options.D: Prescribing strong antibiotics for severe sepsis

explanation: Community health workers are fantastic bridges to the community. They visit homes to make sure babies get their vaccines and moms are recovering nicely.

question: Why is proper waste management so important in a healthcare facility?

options.A: It ensures that doctors spend less time cleaning clinical wards
options.B: It prevents the facility from facing sudden financial bankruptcy
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for any chemical disinfectants
options.D: It protects patients, staff, and handlers from disease and injury

explanation: Spot on! Proper waste control stops dangerous germs and sharp needles from harming anyone inside or outside the hospital.

question: Why is tiopronin often preferred over D-penicillamine in modern practice?

options.A: It generally presents a better and more tolerable side effect profile
options.B: It completely cures the genetic mutation responsible for the condition
options.C: It can be taken just once a year as a slow-release subcutaneous depot
options.D: It works by dissolving calcium oxalate stones instead of cystine

explanation: Tiopronin is much kinder to the patient's body! It causes fewer severe allergic and autoimmune reactions than D-penicillamine, helping patients stick to their treatment.

question: How does dietary counselling differ from Medical Nutrition Therapy?

options.A: There is no real difference between the two terms in clinical practice
options.B: Counselling is only done by surgeons in the operating theatre
options.C: MNT is used exclusively for people who want to lose weight for fashion
options.D: Counselling focuses on general healthy eating, whereas MNT treats complex disease states

explanation: Dietary counselling covers general wellness and basic lifestyle tips, while MNT is an intensive clinical treatment for specific diseases. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T001#GNS227_U7_T001_h5)

question: What are the temporary folds inside the stomach that flatten out when you eat a big meal called?

options.A: Haustra
options.B: Microvilli
options.C: Villi
options.D: Rugae

explanation: Rugae are like little accordion folds in the stomach lining. They let the stomach stretch safely when you enjoy a heavy meal!

question: What is a must-have when introducing a complex new clinical workflow?

options.A: Protected time for staff training during working hours
options.B: Cutting down the number of patient admissions
options.C: Firing senior nurses to save on salaries
options.D: Buying luxury furniture for the breakroom

explanation: Exactly! You can't expect nurses to master new workflows on top of an already crazy shift without giving them dedicated time to learn.

question: Why must a nurse check skin sensation below the level of a spinal cord injury?

options.A: To calculate the daily fluid intake requirements
options.B: To identify areas lacking sensation that are at high risk for unseen injuries
options.C: To check if the patient can still taste and smell normally
options.D: To determine if the patient will ever walk again without assistance

explanation: When patients cannot feel pain or heat, a tiny scratch or hot water can cause severe damage without them even knowing. Regular checks keep them safe!

question: Two clinical supervisors watch the same nursing student perform a procedure and grade them using the same checklist. What are they checking?

options.A: Test-retest validity
options.B: Content consistency
options.C: Inter-rater reliability
options.D: Patient satisfaction

explanation: Inter-rater reliability checks whether different observers get similar scores when using the exact same tool. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T21#GNS224_U1_T21_h7)

question: Where would you usually find a clinical dietitian doing their daily work?

options.A: Inside a hospital or clinic
options.B: Managing a community farming cooperative
options.C: At a national agricultural trade ministry
options.D: Writing policy for a food manufacturing plant

explanation: Clinical dietitians work hand-in-hand with individual patients right inside healthcare facilities like hospitals and clinics.

question: Which organ system uses hormones to regulate slow, long-term body processes?

options.A: The nervous system
options.B: The muscular system
options.C: The endocrine system
options.D: The respiratory system

explanation: Glands in the endocrine system secrete chemical messengers called hormones directly into the bloodstream to control distant target organs over time. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T9#GNS111_U1_T9_h3)

question: What is the primary mechanism of an autoclave in waste treatment?

options.A: Dissolving metal instruments in strong acids
options.B: Burning waste at extremely high open flames
options.C: Freezing biological specimens to sub-zero temperatures
options.D: Steam sterilization under high pressure

explanation: Autoclaves use pressurized steam to kill all infectious agents present in medical waste effectively. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h5)

question: What major feature separates fungi and parasites from bacteria?

options.A: They possess viral capsids instead of cell walls
options.B: They can only survive without oxygen
options.C: They are eukaryotic with a true nucleus
options.D: They lack any form of genetic material

explanation: Unlike bacteria (which are simple prokaryotes), fungi and parasites are eukaryotes—meaning their cells have a proper, organized nucleus, just like human cells do.

question: What is the primary function of synovial fluid inside a joint capsule?

options.A: Fighting off systemic blood infections
options.B: Producing red blood cells for the limb
options.C: Anchoring muscles firmly to the bone
options.D: Lubricating the joint and nourishing cartilage

explanation: Synovial fluid acts as a natural shock absorber and lubricant while feeding the joint cartilage. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h2)

question: Why is talking to a witness so helpful when assessing a seizure?

options.A: Witnesses can prescribe the right medication immediately
options.B: The patient is usually unable to remember or describe the event themselves
options.C: Witnesses know the exact medical history of the patient
options.D: Doctors do not trust tests like the EEG

explanation: Since patients are often blanking out or unconscious during a fit, someone who watched it happen is your best source for piecing together what really went down!

question: What is the primary goal of injection safety practices?

options.A: To make medication administration faster in busy wards
options.B: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing new needles
options.C: To ensure patients experience no pain during injections
options.D: To prevent harm and infections for everyone involved

question: What are the hormone-producing cell clusters located within the pancreas called?

options.A: Gastric mucosal pits
options.B: Hepatic portal nodes

options.D: Acinar cell clusters

question: A patient is dealing with loneliness and money troubles after losing their partner. What do these life events represent?

options.A: Genetic and chromosomal mutations
options.B: Environmental and situational stressors
options.C: Primary endocrine abnormalities
options.D: Congenital brain structural defects

explanation: You nailed it! Things happening in a person's surroundings—like loss, isolation, or financial stress—are situational triggers that can spark depression.

question: Why is it important for a nurse to explain each step before starting a reproductive assessment?

options.A: To distract the patient from physical pain
options.B: To decrease patient anxiety and build trust
options.C: To speed up the total time spent in the room
options.D: To fulfill strict legal billing requirements

explanation: Spot on! Reproductive exams can feel intimidating. Explaining what you are about to do calms nerves and helps the patient trust you.

question: What is a common behavioral sign that someone might be struggling with drug abuse?

options.A: Consistent attendance at routine clinical check-ups
options.B: Sleeping uninterrupted for eight hours each night
options.C: Sudden personality changes and withdrawal from family activities
options.D: Eating balanced meals at regular hours every single day

explanation: Watch out for secrecy, sudden mood swings, and a person pulling away from family and friends. You're learning to spot the clinical signs!

question: Why do you need to watch the needle site extra carefully after drawing blood from someone with severe liver disease?

options.A: Their veins are usually completely collapsed from chronic fluid overload
options.B: Their skin is too fragile to tolerate standard adhesive tape
options.C: They often have poor clotting due to low production of clotting factors
options.D: Local anesthetics used during the draw can cause severe allergic reactions

explanation: You nailed it! A struggling liver can't pump out enough clotting proteins, meaning your patient is at a higher risk of prolonged bleeding or bruising after a needle stick.

question: Why do we actively monitor injection safety devices in the ward?

options.A: To prevent the transmission of bloodborne infections
options.B: To measure the speed of nursing staff during shifts
options.C: To track the monthly financial budget of the pharmacy

explanation: Spot on! Tracking these tools ensures safety devices are used right, keeping both patients and us safe from nasty infections like HIV and hepatitis.

question: Why does giving out too much informal credit to patients hurt a DRF?

options.A: It encourages manufacturers to stop producing generic medicines

question: What is the medical term for pale, greasy, and very foul-smelling stools caused by fats that weren't absorbed?

question: What are the key ingredients of a strong improvement aim statement?

options.D: Nurse manager signature, budget approval, and patient names

question: In which position should you place a patient who is having an upper gastrointestinal endoscopy?

question: Why can't we use standard adult BMI cutoffs to assess health risks in children and teenagers?

options.A: Children's bones are softer, which skews the standard imperial calculation method

explanation: Spot on! Kids and teens grow fast, so their body fat and height change constantly relative to their age and sex. That's why we use special growth charts instead!

question: What is the primary role of a community nurse during a home birth setting?

options.A: To replace traditional birth attendants without community consent

options.C: To document births for statistical purposes only
options.D: To force every laboring mother to relocate to a tertiary hospital immediately

question: What is the general age range for adolescents according to the World Health Organization?

question: A mother visits the clinic with a four-month-old baby and asks about getting pregnant again immediately. What is your best nursing response regarding child health?

question: What is the primary function of the pulmonary circuit?

question: How do traditional food taboos negatively affect community health?

options.B: They prevent vulnerable groups like pregnant women from eating nutrient-dense foods
options.C: They force families to spend all their income on expensive imported foods

question: What is the main difference between anonymity and confidentiality in research?

question: What is a great benefit of using the vaginal route for misoprostol?

options.B: It means you don't need to know how far along the pregnancy is
options.C: It completely stops all cramping pain

question: What is the most important advice a nurse should give a patient taking a multi-week course of antifungal drugs?

options.A: Double the next dose whenever a single daily dose is accidentally missed

question: What is the most important thing for a nurse to check right after giving a nebulizer treatment with a beta-agonist?

options.A: Checking the patient for signs of severe weight gain

question: What is the primary role of autotrophic microbes in natural water bodies?

options.A: Increasing water turbidity and cloudiness

options.D: Dissolving heavy metals in the sediment

question: What does 'vicarious liability' mean for you as a nurse?

options.C: A patient taking legal action directly against the state government
options.D: A doctor supervising medical students during clinical rounds

question: What is meant by 'capacity building' in community health projects?

options.A: Increasing the salary of foreign NGO directors

question: Which condition is the most common immediate complication following a thoracocentesis?

question: Why does very little blood flow through the fetal lungs before birth?

question: What happens to an infant's temperature reading if they are crying or throwing a tantrum?

options.B: It causes the device to show an error code

question: What role does cyclic AMP (cAMP) play in hormone signaling?

options.D: It destroys the cell-surface receptor after use

question: What is an exciting potential use of augmented reality (AR) glasses in nursing care?

options.B: Automatically administering medications through wireless signals

question: Long-term hookworm infection most commonly leads to which major health problem?

question: Why do teenage girls need more dietary iron than young boys of the same age?

question: Which type of equipment requires heavy capital funding in tertiary hospitals?

question: What should a nurse manager focus on during a disciplinary interview?

question: Why are witness accounts particularly helpful during a nursing assessment for syncope?

question: What makes a patient care goal both effective and useful?

question: When inserting a rectal suppository, past which structure must it go to stay in place?

question: What is the safest position for a patient right after a seizure stops?

question: Why must clinicians be very cautious when giving Class IC drugs to a patient with a history of a heart attack?

question: A nurse wants to start a mental health campaign in a rural town. What should she do first regarding community leaders?

options.C: Engage and involve them early to gain community trust and support

question: Who is the target audience for a universal mental health intervention?

question: A patient with a deep, dirty wound hasn't had a tetanus shot in 10 years. The doctor orders a tetanus vaccine AND tetanus immune globulin. Why give the immune globulin?

options.C: To provide immediate, short-term protection against toxins while the vaccine takes effect
options.D: To permanently replace the patient's bone marrow cells with donor tissue

explanation: The immune globulin gives instant borrowed antibodies to fight fast-acting toxins right now, while waiting for the actual vaccine to stimulate the patient's own body to make long-term defense.

question: What term describes the socially constructed roles and behaviors that societies consider appropriate for men and women?

options.A: Sex
options.B: Gender
options.C: Phenotype
options.D: Genotype

explanation: While sex refers to biology, gender represents the social expectations, behaviors, and roles assigned by culture. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T22#GNS225_U5_T22_h2)

question: Which of the following is the first link in the chain of infection?

options.A: Mode of transmission
options.B: Infectious agent
options.C: Portal of entry
options.D: Susceptible host

explanation: The chain always starts with the actual germ or infectious agent itself before it finds a home. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h2)

question: Which blood test is the most specific indicator of heart muscle damage during a heart attack?

options.A: Complete blood count
options.B: Liver function enzymes
options.C: Serum electrolytes
options.D: Cardiac troponin

explanation: Troponin proteins are released directly into the bloodstream when heart muscle cells are injured or die, making it the primary marker for a heart attack. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h5)

question: What does the horizontal axis, or X-axis, typically display on a healthcare bar chart?

options.A: The numerical frequency or percentage
options.B: The financial cost of hospital supplies
options.C: The distinct categories being compared
options.D: The exact date and time of a study

explanation: The X-axis holds the group labels, such as different hospital wards or types of procedures. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T7#GNS217_U4_T7_h2)

question: Why do women pregnant with multiples need extra iron and folic acid supplements?

options.A: To suppress the natural production of amniotic fluid
options.B: To support the massive expansion of blood volume and fetal growth
options.C: To help tighten the pelvic floor muscles before labor
options.D: To prevent the development of gestational diabetes mellitus

explanation: Spot on! Two (or more) babies mean the mum needs way more blood and nutrients to support everyone. Extra supplements help keep deficiency anemia far away.

question: A patient comes in with lower belly pain and a history of pelvic infections. Which tube-related complication should a nurse watch for closely?

options.A: Cervical dilation
options.B: Ovarian hyperstimulation
options.C: Ectopic pregnancy
options.D: Vaginal atrophy

explanation: Brilliant! Scarred fallopian tubes can trap a fertilized egg, leading to an ectopic pregnancy outside the uterus. Always keep an eye out for this!

question: A student nurse uses old patient charts from the archive to study infection rates from last year. What kind of data is this?

options.A: Primary data
options.B: Experimental data
options.C: Secondary data
options.D: Hypothetical data

explanation: Well done! Because the student is using pre-existing records gathered by someone else in the past, it's called secondary data.

question: Why are government subsidies for vulnerable groups so important for achieving UHC?

options.A: They stop international organizations from offering grants
options.B: They allow private hospital owners to become very wealthy
options.C: They protect citizens who cannot afford insurance premiums on their own
options.D: They replace the need for primary health care centers entirely

explanation: Subsidies act as a safety net, ensuring that pregnant mothers, children, and the elderly aren't left behind just because they have little money.

question: What does a 24-hour dietary recall ask the patient to do?

options.A: Weigh every meal on a digital scale for a full week
options.B: List all food and drink consumed over the past day
options.C: Write down future grocery shopping lists in advance
options.D: Fast completely for 24 hours before a blood test

explanation: Easy peasy! A 24-hour recall simply asks the patient to remember and list everything they ate and drank during the last 24 hours.

question: Which term describes a joint that allows no movement at all?

options.A: Diarthrosis
options.B: Synarthrosis
options.C: Amphiarthrosis
options.D: Synovial

explanation: Spot on! 'Synarthrosis' refers to fixed, immovable joints, like the sutures between the bones of your skull.

question: In family planning, what does the term LARC stand for?

options.A: Late Adult Regular Cycling
options.B: Local Adolescent Reproductive Care
options.C: Long-Acting Reversible Contraception
options.D: Low-Altered Reproductive Capacity

explanation: Well done! LARC methods like implants and IUDs give great birth control protection for a long time without needing daily remembering.

question: Under Nigerian law, when is an abortion legally allowed?

options.A: Whenever requested by the male partner or husband
options.B: Only when necessary to save the life of the pregnant woman
options.C: In all cases involving financial hardship or unemployment
options.D: Whenever the woman decides she is not ready for a child

explanation: Spot on. Nigerian law is quite strict and generally permits termination only if the mother's life is in direct danger.

question: What is the primary difference between an arranged marriage and a forced marriage?

options.A: The involvement of religious leaders
options.B: The age of the individuals getting married
options.C: The right to refuse and give full consent
options.D: The geographic location of the ceremony

explanation: In an arranged marriage, the individuals still have the freedom to say no, whereas a forced marriage happens without their consent. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T10#GNS312_U1_T10_h1)

question: Why must nurses look beyond the individual adolescent patient during clinical assessments?

options.A: Hospital guidelines require at least three relatives to be present at all times.
options.B: Biological markers can only be measured accurately when family is near.
options.C: Teenagers are rarely able to speak for themselves during medical visits.
options.D: Family and community networks heavily shape a teenager's health choices.

explanation: Because a teenager's environment directly impacts their health habits and recovery, understanding their social circle is essential for effective care. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T20#GNS312_U3_T20_h1)

question: How is an idiosyncratic drug reaction different from a regular side effect?

options.A: It only happens when a patient takes an overdose of medicine.
options.B: It can be easily predicted by checking standard blood test results.
options.C: It is a mild response that always goes away without any treatment.
options.D: It is completely unpredictable and does not depend on the drug dose.

explanation: Think of an idiosyncratic reaction as a surprise response! Unlike normal side effects that we expect, these happen out of nowhere due to a patient's unique body makeup, not because of a high dose. You've got this!

question: What is the single best way to stop infections from spreading in any healthcare setting?

options.A: Wearing sterile gowns for every procedure
options.B: Performing proper hand hygiene
options.C: Administering prophylactic antibiotics
options.D: Using disposable plastic trays

explanation: Simple handwashing or alcohol rubbing is your superpower against hospital infections. It removes germs picked up from patients and surroundings instantly.

question: Which medical intervention is commonly used to break the cycle of severe pain and tension in labour?

options.A: Epidural analgesia
options.B: Oral iron supplementation
options.C: Routine amniotomy
options.D: Intravenous antibiotics

explanation: An epidural blocks pain signals so an exhausted, tense mum can finally relax and get some much-needed rest.

question: Which rare, serious skin and tissue condition can develop in patients with bad kidney function who receive gadolinium contrast?

options.A: Acute radiation sickness
options.B: Chronic bone marrow failure
options.C: Malignant hyperthermia crisis
options.D: Nephrogenic systemic fibrosis

explanation: Well done! Gadolinium can trigger this serious condition in patients whose kidneys are struggling to filter waste.

question: Under the WHO medical rules, what does a Category 4 classification mean for a contraceptive method?

options.A: The benefits outweigh the risks in most cases
options.B: There are no restrictions on using the method
options.C: The method can be used with routine monitoring
options.D: The method represents an unacceptable health risk

explanation: Category 4 means 'Stop!' — the condition is too dangerous, and the contraceptive must not be used because it puts the client's health at serious risk.

question: What is the main underlying cause of osteoarthritis?

options.A: An autoimmune attack on the joint lining
options.B: A sudden bacterial infection in the bone marrow
options.C: Wear and tear breakdown of joint cartilage over time
options.D: A total lack of synovial fluid from birth

explanation: You got it! Osteoarthritis is primarily a degenerative condition where the protective cartilage cushions wear down over the years.

question: What do we call a disease that is always present at a steady, expected level in a specific area?

options.A: Outbreak
options.B: Pandemic
options.C: Endemic
options.D: Epidemic

explanation: Think of an endemic disease as having a permanent, predictable home in a certain region over time. You've got this!

question: Which Nigerian law provides broad legal protection against domestic violence and sexual assault at the federal level?

options.A: Violence Against Persons Prohibition (VAPP) Act
options.B: Criminal Code Public Order Act
options.C: National Health Insurance Authority Act
options.D: Nursing and Midwifery Registration Act

explanation: You nailed it! The VAPP Act is a landmark federal law that criminalizes different forms of GBV and protects survivors.

question: What is the most important ingredient for any healthcare team to work well together?

options.A: Strict orders given only by physicians
options.B: Independent work without sharing notes
options.C: Focusing solely on hospital procedures
options.D: Mutual respect among all team members

explanation: Great thinking! Teamwork only works when everyone values what each person brings to the table.

question: What is the primary goal of geriatric home health care?

options.A: To replace family members in daily care duties
options.B: To provide permanent 24-hour nursing supervision
options.C: To maintain or improve functional independence
options.D: To eliminate the need for primary care doctors

explanation: The main objective of bringing healthcare services into the home is to help older adults stay as independent and functional as possible in familiar surroundings. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T1#GNS324_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why does an undescended testicle often lead to problems with future fertility?

options.A: The testicle fails to receive any blood supply throughout childhood and adolescence
options.B: Immune cells easily cross the blood-testis barrier and destroy the abnormal organ
options.C: The vas deferens naturally attaches to the wrong structure during development
options.D: Higher core body temperature inside the abdomen damages the delicate sperm-producing tissue

explanation: Testes need a cooler environment outside the main body cavity; staying inside the abdomen causes permanent heat damage. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h3)

question: Why do doctors often use laparoscopy to look closely at the fallopian tubes?

options.A: It requires no anesthesia and is done at the bedside
options.B: It completely cures all tubal blockages
options.C: It uses high-frequency sound waves to measure organ density
options.D: It lets the surgeon see the pelvic organs directly with a camera

explanation: A laparoscope is a tiny lighted camera that gives the surgeon a clear, direct view of what is going on inside the pelvis. You're mastering this topic!

question: What is the main job of an Electronic Health Record (EHR) in the hospital?

options.A: Tracking hospital supply inventory and ordering new medical equipment
options.B: Managing staff work schedules and payroll calculations
options.C: Providing entertainment options for clients staying overnight
options.D: Serving as a digital version of a client's comprehensive medical chart

explanation: An EHR is simply your patient's complete medical history, lab results, and notes kept safely in one digital folder. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h2)

question: How does a transformational nurse leader typically influence their team?

options.A: By making all clinical decisions without consulting anyone
options.B: By threatening disciplinary action for late shift arrivals
options.C: By inspiring them with a shared vision for better care
options.D: By leaving them alone to figure out tasks themselves

explanation: Transformational leaders focus on motivation, inspiration, and elevating the team's commitment to patient care. [learn more](GST321_U3_T3#GST321_U3_T3_h5)

question: If a community health nurse wants to help mothers fight iron-deficiency anemia using local foods, which food group should she focus on?

options.A: Clear fruit juices with added artificial colors
options.B: Highly refined starches and sugary beverages
options.C: Saturated cooking oils and bottled water
options.D: Dark green leafy vegetables and local grains

explanation: You nailed it! Dark green veggies and whole local grains are packed with the iron needed to build strong, healthy red blood cells.

question: How does the NAFDAC Yellow Form system mostly gather its safety data?

options.A: Mandatory daily electronic tracking of every patient
options.B: Telephone interviews conducted by pharmaceutical reps
options.C: Automated computer alerts generated by hospital pharmacies
options.D: Spontaneous reporting by healthcare workers

explanation: The yellow form system depends on caring clinicians and nurses voluntarily filling it out whenever they notice a strange reaction in a patient.

question: At what angle should you typically insert the venepuncture needle into the skin?

options.A: 45 to 60 degrees
options.B: 15 to 30 degrees
options.C: 5 to 10 degrees
options.D: 75 to 90 degrees

explanation: A gentle angle of 15 to 30 degrees lets you slide smoothly into the vein without accidentally poking right through the other side!

question: You hear a call bell ring, but right at that moment, another patient starts struggling to breathe. What should you do first?

options.A: Finish charting at the desk before responding to either
options.B: Assess the patient who is struggling to breathe
options.C: Answer the call bell immediately to find out what is needed
options.D: Ask a visitor to check on the patient in the room

explanation: Brilliant! ABC comes first. A breathing difficulty is a life-threatening emergency that always beats a general call bell.

question: What defines an epidemic compared to an endemic disease?

options.A: Only children living in rural villages catch the illness
options.B: Cases rise significantly above the normal baseline level
options.C: Infections disappear entirely during the dry season
options.D: The disease spreads globally to multiple continents

explanation: An epidemic occurs when the frequency of a disease surges well past what is normally expected for that area and time. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T14#GNS313_U1_T14_h2)

question: Why do many women with vulval tumours come to the hospital quite late?

options.A: Pain is usually so severe that patients refuse to leave home
options.B: Doctors routinely screen for vulval growths during annual exams
options.C: Symptoms are mistaken for common infections or cause embarrassment
options.D: The condition always spreads rapidly without any warning signs

explanation: You got it! Many patients delay coming in because they feel shy or mistake early signs for a simple skin irritation or infection.

question: Which type of cell division is responsible for producing sperm and egg cells?

options.A: Meiosis
options.B: Osmosis
options.C: Binary fission
options.D: Mitosis

explanation: Meiosis reduces the chromosome number by half, creating specialized reproductive cells needed for sexual reproduction. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T5#GNS111_U1_T5_h5)

question: Why is emotional and psychological support so important for patients dealing with amenorrhoea?

options.A: Emotional support replaces the need for any complex diagnostic blood testing
options.B: Patients will refuse all physical examinations unless their anxiety is treated first
options.C: Psychological stress is the only scientifically proven cause of primary amenorrhoea
options.D: Changes in menstrual patterns often create strong emotional distress regarding identity and fertility

explanation: Not seeing a regular period can be really scary for a young woman, often triggering worries about her womanhood and future family.

question: Why do skeletal muscles get bigger when someone does heavy weightlifting regularly?

options.A: Cellular hypertrophy occurs due to increased functional demand
options.B: Metaplasia transforms fat tissue directly into muscle tissue
options.C: Atrophy removes damaged proteins to make space for fluid
options.D: Hyperplasia creates brand new muscle fibers in the tissue

explanation: You're crushing this! Since muscle fibers don't easily make brand new cells, the existing cells bulk up (hypertrophy) to handle the heavy workload.

question: What is a major challenge that stops agricultural and food policies from succeeding?

options.A: Having too many trained nurses working as policy makers
options.B: Inadequate funding and a lack of follow-through when governments change
options.C: People refusing to eat locally grown foods
options.D: Having too much cold storage in every single village

explanation: Frequent political shifts and poor funding often leave great agricultural policies unfinished.

question: What is another common name for the normal bacteria and microbes living on and inside the human body?

options.A: Human microbiota
options.B: Somatic organisms
options.C: Pathogenic colonies
options.D: Acellular particles

explanation: You've got this! 'Human microbiota' is just the scientific term for the friendly community of microbes that call our bodies home. Every healthy person has them!

question: A clinic finds 20 people with malaria in a town of 4,000 residents. What is the prevalence per 1,000 people?
explanation: Divide 20 by 4,000 to get 0.005, then multiply by 1,000 to get 5 per 1,000 people. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h3)

question: Why are drugs like morphine classified under strict schedules even though they have medical uses?

options.A: They carry a high risk of dependence and abuse
options.B: They are extremely expensive to import from abroad
options.C: They can only be administered by specialized surgeons
options.D: They lose their potency very quickly in storage

explanation: Even though they relieve severe pain, strong opioids can easily lead to addiction if not closely monitored. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T13#GNS122_U1_T13_h4)

question: What happens at the cellular level right when a seizure starts?

options.A: Excessive neuronal excitation combined with a failure of inhibition
options.B: Massive overproduction of cerebrospinal fluid in the ventricles
options.C: Rapid destruction of myelin sheaths along peripheral nerves
options.D: Complete depletion of glucose stores within glial cells

explanation: Seizures happen when brain signals become too excited and the brain's natural 'brakes' (inhibition) fail to slow them down. You are building strong clinical instincts!
